title: Best-of-N Sampling as an Attack: How Many Samples Until Any Harmful Prompt Succeeds?

original_idea.body: For a fixed harmful prompt set, sample each prompt N times at deployment temperature, record the minimum N at which a harmful completion appears, and report the N-to-break distribution across models and categories.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying best-of-N jailbreak risk is a real deployment-robustness finding but targets misuse rather than a specific loss-of-control scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure repeated sampling plus StrongREJECT grading; the most beginner-accessible experiment possible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped N-to-break distribution with a crisp metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Doable externally but best-of-N jailbreaking is well-explored by Anthropic and others.

low_compute.reasoning: Heavy sampling (N up to hundreds) but on open models, single GPU.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Best-of-N jailbreaking is an established, published finding.
